paragraphs.text: Abstract. A Bi2WO6/BiOI heterojunction photocatalyst achieved 91.8 percent removal of ciprofloxacin within 120 min under visible light (lambda greater than 420 nm).
The composite was prepared by a solvothermal method at 160 degrees C for 12 h, using ethylene glycol as the solvent.

Under the same visible-light irradiation, the Bi2WO6/BiOI composite removed 92.5 percent of ciprofloxacin (10 mg/L) within 120 min, compared with 54.0 percent for pristine Bi2WO6 and 61.2 percent for pristine BiOI.
Cycling tests over five runs showed no significant loss of activity; however, the release of dissolved bismuth during irradiation was not measured, so potential leaching cannot be excluded.
Trapping experiments identified holes as the main reactive species for ciprofloxacin degradation.
Table 1. Removal rates: Bi2WO6/BiOI 92.5 percent, Bi2WO6 54.0 percent, BiOI 61.2 percent; TOC removal reached 47.8 percent after 120 min.
The apparent rate constant was 0.023 per min for the composite, 0.008 per min for Bi2WO6 and 0.010 per min for BiOI.
